ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (39) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form); blocks 4, 37, 38 had no website counterpart and were translated fresh.

Tyutchev's “Silentium!” is translated line by line, unrhymed, from the text as printed here, which differs in places from Tyutchev's usual text («И всходят и зайдут оне, / Как звезды ясные в ночи», 'Both rise and set, / Like clear stars in the night'). «Изреченная» (izrechennaya, 'uttered') in the poem is kept distinct from «высказать» (vyskazat', 'express') in section 2.

Source observation: [15] «Взрывая, возмутить ключи» has the infinitive «возмутить» ('to stir up') where Tyutchev's poem has «возмутишь» ('you will stir up'); probably a one-letter slip, translated as 'you will muddy'
Source observation: [24] the section number 2 is set as an italic text line «*2*» rather than as a plain number; kept as printed
